\title{The Conditional Partition-Ratio Frontier for State-Weighted $SU(2)$ Control}
\author{}
\date{}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
We reduce the remaining one-scale nonlinear problem to a single uniform
weighted partition-function inequality.  The reduction is exact for every
finite compact positive conditional kernel.  Two counterexamples show why a
local action charge and a pointwise good formula are insufficient: entropy
and retained-state normalization must be controlled together.
\end{abstract}

\section{Exact conditional identity}
For retained state $s$, let $w_s(f)>0$ be the conditional fiber weight and
split the compact fiber into $G_s\sqcup B_s$.  With next-state map $\tau$, set
\[
 Z_G(s)=\int_{G_s}w_s(f)\,df,\quad
 Z_B(s)=\int_{B_s}w_s(f)\,df,
\]
\[
 B_V(s)=\int_{B_s}w_s(f)V(\tau(s,f))\,df.
\]

\begin{theorem}
The exact weighted bad row of the normalized conditional kernel is
\[
 q_V(s)=\frac{B_V(s)}{(Z_G(s)+Z_B(s))V(s)}.
\]
If, uniformly in $s$,
\[
 Z_G(s)\ge e^{-\ell}\overline Z_G(s),\qquad
 B_V(s)\le e^{-F}\overline Z_G(s)V(s),
\]
then $q_V(s)\le e^{\ell-F}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The identity follows by inserting the normalized kernel
$w_s/(Z_G+Z_B)$.  For the bound, drop the nonnegative $Z_B$ from the
denominator and apply the two hypotheses.
\end{proof}

At the Stage 25 split, the residual ceiling is
$r=0.001215138750921001$ and $\ell=2.40009685\cdot10^{-5}$.  Hence it is
sufficient to prove
\[
 F>\ell-\log r=6.712921011389365.
\]

\section{Why deterministic charge is insufficient}
Give the good channel one microstate of weight one.  Give the bad channel
$M=\lceil e^{10}\rceil=22027$ microstates, each with action charge ten and
weight $e^{-10}$.  Then
\[
 Z_B=Me^{-10}=1.00002425,\qquad
 \mathbb P(B)=0.50000606.
\]
Thus action energy without entropy is not a free-energy estimate.

A second two-state example takes
$(Z_G,Z_B)=(1,\varepsilon)$ in one retained state and
$(\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ in another.  Pointwise good formulas may be the
same, yet the bad probabilities tend to zero and $1/2$.  The supremum over
positive-mass retained states is essential.

\section{First unproved inequality}
The constructive target is now explicit: uniformly in finite volume,
positive-mass exposure history, retained state, and defect channel, prove
\[
 \frac{B_V(s)}{\overline Z_G(s)V(s)}\le e^{-F_*},
 \qquad F_*>6.71292101139.
\]
The finite conditional kernel exists by compactness and positivity, but this
uniform free-energy inequality is not established.  Therefore one-scale
basin entry, RG iteration, continuum construction, and the Hamiltonian mass
gap remain open.
